ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a describing word

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. run

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Fluency in Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Fluency in Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Fluency in Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Fluency in Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Fluency in Speaking.

4. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading - Fluency ● Using fluency strategies (previewing pr edicti, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading - Fluency ● Using fluency strategies (previewing pr edicti.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading - Fluency ● Using fluency strategies (previewing pr edicti.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading - Fluency ● Using fluency strategies (previewing pr edicti.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading - Fluency ● Using fluency strategies (previewing pr edicti.

5. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes ● Nouns: (regular/ irregular; collective, comp, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes ● Nouns: (regular/ irregular; collective, comp.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes ● Nouns: (regular/ irregular; collective, comp.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes ● Nouns: (regular/ irregular; collective, comp.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes ● Nouns: (regular/ irregular; collective, comp.

6. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading ● Previewing and selecting and a non- literary t, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading ● Previewing and selecting and a non- literary t.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading ● Previewing and selecting and a non- literary t.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading ● Previewing and selecting and a non- literary t.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading ● Previewing and selecting and a non- literary t.

7. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling Rules and Commonly Confused Words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling Rules and Commonly Confused Words.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling Rules and Commonly Confused Words.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling Rules and Commonly Confused Words.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling Rules and Commonly Confused Words.

8. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

9. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word classes: Main and Auxiliary Verbs ● Primary auxiliarie, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word classes: Main and Auxiliary Verbs ● Primary auxiliarie.

10. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. going

11. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Sentence Skills: Sentence Fluency ● Sentence fragments ● Misplaced, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Sentence Skills: Sentence Fluency ● Sentence fragments ● Misplaced.

   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● Recognising a speaker’s attitu.

----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening ● Listening for essential infor and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 4.1.2 Conversational Skills: Speaking Fluency ● Diagraphs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Conversational Skills: Speaking Fluency ● Diagraphs with silent letters: bt - de and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 4.2.1 Study Skills: Library Skills ● Locating relevant print and digital and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. D — run

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Fluency in Speaking.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading - Fluency ● Using fluency strategies (previewing pr edicti.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading ● Previewing and selecting and a non- literary t.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling Rules and Commonly Confused Words.

8. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word classes: Main and Auxiliary Verbs ● Primary auxiliarie.

10. B — went

11. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Sentence Skills: Sentence Fluency ● Sentence fragments ● Misplaced.

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● Recognising a speaker’s attitu.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening ● Listening for essential infor; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 4.1.2 Conversational Skills: Speaking Fluency ● Diagraphs; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Conversational Skills: Speaking Fluency ● Diagraphs with silent letters: bt - de; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 4.2.1 Study Skills: Library Skills ● Locating relevant print and digital; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
